data.gender_notes: Arkarsh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arkarsh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'arka' meaning chariot and 'rish' meaning lord. In Hindu mythology, Arkarsh is the name of the charioteer of the sun god Surya. He is responsible for guiding the sun across the sky each day. The name Arkarsh carries the meaning “Lord of the Chariot” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arkarsh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the chariot and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The sun is regarded as a symbol of power, energy, and renewal. Arkarsh, as the charioteer, represents guidance, direction, and the journey towards enlightenment. The name might bring to mind images of strength, discipline, and determination, reflecting the traditional values of Hindu culture.

historical_references.reference: Arkarsh was a commander in the army of the Chalukya king, Kirtivarman II Anandaraya (544-597 AD). He is best known for his role in the Battle of Vatapi, where the Chalukyas successfully defended their capital city against the invading Western Gangas.

Arkarsh is also mentioned in the 12th-century Indian epic, the 'Mahabharata', where he is described as the charioteer of Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers. In this context, Arkarsh plays a crucial role in the Battle of Kurukshetra, helping Bhima defeat his adversaries.
